01

The bay

I started shaping in 2009 because I couldn’t afford the board I wanted, and kept going because the third one was better than the one in the shop. Seventeen years later I’m still in the same neighborhood, still sweeping foam dust off the same floor.

I shape about forty boards a year. I could do more if I hired someone or bought a machine, but then they wouldn’t be my boards, and you can get those anywhere. Every blank gets skinned, foiled, and finished by me, with your name and your wave written in pencil on the stringer.

Most of what I shape gets ridden between the harbor and the county line. If you surf C-Street, the point at Pitas, or Rincon on the good winter days — I’ve shaped for your wave a few hundred times.

— Walt

The boards

Model Dims Glassing What it’s for

The Pier Rat Twin-keel fish

5′6″–6′2″ × 20–21″

4 + 4 / 4 oz · tint optional

For the summer south swells that never quite get there. Flat, fast, forgiving.

The C-Street Single-fin egg · midlength

6′8″–7′6″ × 21–21 ½″

6 + 4 / 6 oz volan

The board I ride most. Paddles like a log, turns off the tail, glides through the flat sections at the point.

The Rincon Log Square-tail noserider

9′2″–9′8″ × 22 ½–23″

Double 8 oz volan · gloss & polish

Fifty-fifty rails, nose concave, heavy on purpose. Built to trim, not to be carried easily.

The Overhead Step-up · round pin

6′6″–7′2″ × 19 ½–20″

6 + 4 / 4 oz · clear only

For the six days a winter when Rincon is doing the thing. You’ll be glad you waited.

These are starting points, not a catalog. Every board is shaped to your height, weight, wave, and honesty about your paddling. If you want something that isn’t on this list, ask — the weird ones are my favorite orders.

03

How it works

01

We talk

Call, email, or come by the bay. Bring your current board. I’ll ask where you surf, how often, and what you want the board to do that your last one didn’t.

02

You wait

About six months. I take a small deposit and put you in the book. I’ll call you a few weeks out to confirm dims — people change their minds, and that’s fine.

03

I shape

A week of evenings with the planer and the screens. Your dims go on the stringer in pencil. You’re welcome to come watch the skinning pass.

04

Glassing

Laminated two blocks away by the same glasser I’ve used for a decade. Volan, tints, and gloss coats take longer. Worth it every time.

05

Pick-up

You come get it. We look it over together, I tell you how to break it in, and you tell me how it goes at the point. Bring wax.

The list

The list is the list. No exceptions, no rush fees.

Email me with your height, weight, where you surf, and what you’re riding now. I answer everything myself, usually in the evening after the dust settles. If the surf is good it might take a day or two.
